foyer.title: The little bell
lines: A low bell rings. A water dish tips at the edge of the Butler’s tray.
A little hatch opens beside the counter. A tiny towel hangs from the Butler’s head.
foyer.recap: A little service bell rings. The Butler’s water dish is tipping beside an open hatch.

choices.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
lines: You steady the dish. The Butler catches the tray beneath it without spilling a drop.

lines.speaker: The Butler
lines.text: Excellent timing. Animals dislike a breakfast served vertically.

lines: He sets the water by the hatch. An unseen nose sniffs; the dish slides inside.
He leaves the towel on his head until the drinking stops.
choices.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

choices.label: Point out the waiting hatch.
lines: You point to the hatch. The Butler catches the dish with his free hand and turns the tray.

lines.speaker: The Butler
lines.text: The breakfast bell. Supper? The clock is unhelpful. They are fed.

lines: A nose sniffs at the water. The dish slides inside, and quiet lapping follows.
The towel stays on his head. For once, something else comes first.
choices.recap: You pointed out the waiting hatch. The Butler caught the dish and served the animal its water.

choices.label: Give the Butler room.
lines: You leave room beside the tray. The Butler catches the tipping dish without losing a drop.

lines.speaker: The Butler
lines.text: The animals’ water. I do remember the important parts.

lines: He serves it through the hatch. A nose sniffs, and the dish slides inside.
The tiny towel remains on his head until the drinking stops.
choices.recap: You gave the Butler room. He caught the dish and tended the animal behind the hatch.

nursery.title: A busy hat
lines: The Governess reaches toward the soldier’s crooked duster hat.
The soldier pats its hat, then points the feathers toward a dusty sleeve.
nursery.recap: The Governess wants to straighten the hat. The soldier has a job for it.

choices.label: Point to the dusty sleeve.
lines: You point to the dust. The Governess lowers her sleeve within the soldier’s reach.
The crooked hat dusts it beautifully. The soldier pats the hat again.

lines.speaker: The Governess
lines.text: Oh. You were busy.

lines: She leaves the hat alone and offers her other sleeve.
choices.recap: You pointed out the dust. The Governess let the soldier keep its hat and finish its job.

choices.label: Clear a little space on the table.
lines: You slide an empty spool aside. The soldier steps into the space and dusts the Governess’s sleeve.

lines.speaker: The Governess
lines.text: I see. You require working room.

lines: She turns her other sleeve toward it. The hat remains proudly crooked.
choices.recap: You cleared working space. The soldier kept its hat, and the Governess offered both sleeves for dusting.

choices.label: Watch what the soldier does.
lines: You wait. The soldier ducks beneath the Governess’s hand and dusts her sleeve.
Her hand stops above the crooked hat.

lines.speaker: The Governess
lines.text: Oh. You were busy.

lines: She offers the other sleeve instead of straightening anything.
choices.recap: You watched. The soldier showed what its hat was for, and the Governess left it alone.

sleeping-quarters.title: From the inside
lines: A small paw reaches beneath the curtain toward its dangling cord.
The Beast’s foot blocks the gap. The cord stops just short of the paw.
sleeping-quarters.recap: The occupant is reaching for a curtain cord it cannot quite reach.

choices.label: Lower the loose end of the cord.
lines: You lower the loose end. The Beast shifts its foot aside, and the paw takes the cord.
The curtain opens a little, then closes again.

lines.speaker: The Bedframe Beast
lines.text: An excellent hiding place. It works both ways.

lines: The cord stays within reach on the inside.
choices.recap: You lowered the cord. The Beast cleared the gap, and the occupant can now open or close its own curtain.

choices.label: Show the Beast where its foot is.
lines: You point to the blocked gap. The Beast looks down.

lines.speaker: The Bedframe Beast
lines.text: That foot again. Always somewhere.

lines: It moves the foot and lowers the cord. The paw opens the curtain a little, then closes it.
The Beast keeps the gap clear and the cord within reach.
choices.recap: You showed the blocked gap. The Beast moved its foot and gave the occupant control of the curtain.

choices.label: Give the little paw room.
lines: You wait clear of the curtain. The paw reaches again.
The Beast notices, shifts its foot, and lowers the cord into the paw’s reach.
The curtain opens a little, then closes.

lines.speaker: The Bedframe Beast
lines.text: A very good place to choose to hide.

choices.recap: You gave the occupant room. The Beast cleared the gap and left the cord where the paw could reach it.

kitchens-cellars.title: One plain spoon
lines: A plain spoon lies beneath the Recipe Board, beside a bowl of soup.
The Confectioner reaches for its icing bag.
kitchens-cellars.recap: A useful plain spoon is beside the soup. The Confectioner is considering icing it.

choices.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
lines: You move the spoon beside the bowl. The Confectioner gives the soup one careful stir.

lines.speaker: The Confectioner
lines.text: No lumps. No sprinkles. Remarkable.

lines: It sets the icing bag down and places the plain spoon safely apart from the decorations.
choices.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

choices.label: Ask, “Can it stir already?”

lines.speaker: The Confectioner
lines.text: Without improvements? A bold experiment.

lines: It stirs the soup. The spoon does exactly what a spoon should do.
The icing bag goes down. The plain spoon goes into its own clean place.

lines.speaker: The Confectioner
lines.text: Do not sprinkle the experiment.

choices.recap: You asked whether the spoon already worked. The Confectioner tested it and kept it plain.

choices.label: Watch the spoon for a moment.
lines: You wait. The Confectioner lifts the spoon with the hand that was reaching for the icing.
It tries one stir. Then another.

lines.speaker: The Confectioner
lines.text: Keep this one. We may need to stir something.

lines: It leaves the spoon plain and puts the icing aside.
choices.recap: You watched. The Confectioner discovered that the plain spoon worked and left it that way.

greenhouse.title: The light over there
lines: A seedling leans toward a patch of light beyond the vines. Its pot nudges the nearest vine.
The Conservatory makes a brighter patch beside the pot. The seedling keeps leaning the other way.
greenhouse.recap: The seedling is reaching for light beyond the vines, despite the brighter light offered beside it.

choices.label: Point along the seedling’s chosen direction.
lines: You trace the direction of the leaning leaves with one finger.
The Conservatory’s leaves turn to follow. Its vines uncurl from the little path.
The pot shuffles into the light it wanted. A new vine reaches after it, then curls aside.
choices.recap: You showed the seedling’s direction. The Conservatory cleared the path, and the seedling moved into its chosen light.

choices.label: Move a fallen leaf off the little path.
lines: You slide the loose leaf aside. The pot shuffles into that small clear space, still facing the farther light.
The Conservatory uncurls the next vine, then the next.
The seedling reaches its chosen patch. The vines leave its path clear.
choices.recap: You cleared a small part of the path. The Conservatory opened the rest, and the seedling reached its chosen light.

choices.label: Give the seedling time.
lines: You wait. The seedling nudges the vine once more, then leans toward the same distant patch.
At last, the vines uncurl. The pot shuffles into the light it wanted.
A new leaf reaches after it, then folds aside.
choices.recap: You waited for the seedling. The Conservatory opened its path and left it in its chosen light.

graveyard.title: The part that stays
lines: The Groundskeeper opens a book at WENT HOME. A paw-shaped smudge covers part of the writing.
His polishing cloth pauses above the smudge.
graveyard.recap: A familiar pawprint marks the record of an animal who went home. The Groundskeeper is about to polish the page.

choices.label: Point gently to the pawprint.
lines: You point to the little shape. The Groundskeeper lowers his cloth beside it.

lines.speaker: The Groundskeeper of Names
lines.text: This one always sat on my writing.

lines: He dusts around the print and leaves it untouched.

lines.speaker: The Groundskeeper of Names
lines.text: That part can stay.

choices.recap: You pointed to the pawprint. The Groundskeeper remembered its visitor and kept the mark.

choices.label: Ask, “What were they like?”

lines.speaker: The Groundskeeper of Names
lines.text: Very interested in whatever page I needed next.

lines: His cloth moves away from the pawprint.

lines.speaker: The Groundskeeper of Names
lines.text: This one always sat on my writing.

lines: He leaves the familiar smudge on the record of going home.
choices.recap: You asked about the animal. The Groundskeeper shared a familiar habit and left its pawprint in the book.

choices.label: Sit with the quiet moment.
lines: You stay quietly beside the open book. The Groundskeeper looks at the smudge again.

lines.speaker: The Groundskeeper of Names
lines.text: This one always sat on my writing.

lines: He puts down the cloth.

lines.speaker: The Groundskeeper of Names
lines.text: That part can stay.

choices.recap: You shared the quiet moment. The Groundskeeper remembered the animal and kept its pawprint.

study-library.title: A place for the replies
lines: Unanswered return requests spill from a drawer. An empty outgoing tray waits on the desk.
The Archivist opens a tiny drawer and hesitates.
study-library.recap: The return requests need an answer. The outgoing tray is empty, and the Archivist is reconsidering where to put them.

choices.label: Bring the outgoing tray within reach.
lines: You slide the outgoing tray closer. The Archivist moves the requests into it.
They write I WAS WRONG on the tiny drawer, look at the remaining pile, and open a cupboard instead.

lines.speaker: The Archivist
lines.text: Room to improve. Quite a lot of room.

lines: The last requests need a second outgoing tray.
choices.recap: You brought the outgoing tray closer. The Archivist sent the requests onward and made a cupboard for corrections.

choices.label: Set the loose requests together on the desk.
lines: You gather the loose pages into a readable stack. The Archivist checks each request before placing it in the outgoing tray.

lines.speaker: The Archivist
lines.text: A small drawer for my mistakes should—

lines: They see how much of the stack remains and open a cupboard marked I WAS WRONG.
The requests fill two outgoing trays.
choices.recap: You gathered the requests. The Archivist checked them, sent them onward, and made a cupboard for corrections.

choices.label: Wait while the Archivist reads.
lines: You give the Archivist time to read the unanswered requests.
They write I WAS WRONG on the tiny drawer, then look at the pile.

lines.speaker: The Archivist
lines.text: A cupboard.

lines: The requests move into the outgoing tray. It needs a second tray.
choices.recap: You waited while the Archivist read. The requests went to outgoing trays, and the corrections gained a cupboard.

attic-observatory.title: One thing happening now
lines: Warning threads slacken across the rafters. A loose telescope starts to roll along a tilted table.
An empty stand waits beside the table. The Watcher’s eyes dart between the telescope and a hundred tangled forecasts.
attic-observatory.recap: A telescope is starting to roll while the Watcher watches too many possible dangers at once.

choices.label: Point out the rolling telescope.
lines: You point. One quick thread catches the telescope before it reaches the edge.

lines.speaker: The Watcher in the Rafters
lines.text: That one was happening.

lines: It keeps that thread in place and loosens the other warnings. The way onward becomes visible.
choices.recap: You pointed out the real movement. The Watcher caught the telescope and cleared the other warning threads from the route.

choices.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
lines: You show the Watcher the empty telescope stand beside you.
A quick thread catches the rolling telescope and settles it into the stand.

lines.speaker: The Watcher in the Rafters
lines.text: A place to put it. Yes.

lines: It loosens the other warnings, leaving room to see the way onward.
choices.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

choices.label: Give the Watcher room to act.
lines: You keep clear of the table. The Watcher catches the telescope with one quick thread.

lines.speaker: The Watcher in the Rafters
lines.text: That one was happening.

lines: It keeps that thread and loosens the others. The way onward appears between the warnings.
choices.recap: You left room. The Watcher caught the telescope and cleared the other warnings from the route.

lampworks.title: A useful place to shine
lines: A little lamp swings toward the dark threshold. The Lamplighter reaches after it.
An empty hook waits beside the way onward.
lampworks.recap: A lamp is leaning toward the dark threshold, where an empty hook offers a place to shine.

choices.label: Point out the empty hook.
lines: You point to the hook. The Lamplighter lifts the leaning lamp onto it.
The beam reveals a small pawprint at the threshold.

lines.speaker: The Lamplighter
lines.text: Lighting the way. That is a position.

lines: The smaller lamp leans toward the door too. The doorway light stays in place.
choices.recap: You showed the hook. The Lamplighter placed a lamp there to light the way onward.

choices.label: Step out of the lamp’s beam.
lines: You move clear of the beam. Its light reaches the threshold, and the lamp leans farther that way.
The Lamplighter follows its aim and sets it on the waiting hook.

lines.speaker: The Lamplighter
lines.text: Oh. You were lighting something.

lines: The little lamp keeps its useful place by the door.
choices.recap: You cleared the beam. The Lamplighter followed the lamp’s aim and gave it a place by the threshold.

choices.label: Watch where the lamp turns.
lines: You wait. The lamp keeps swinging toward the dark way onward.
The Lamplighter reaches after it, then lifts it onto the hook there.
The beam finds a small pawprint. A smaller lamp leans after it.

lines.speaker: The Lamplighter
lines.text: One at a time. I see the position now.

choices.recap: You watched the lamp’s direction. The Lamplighter set it by the threshold, where it stayed to light the way.

ballroom.title: One goodbye
lines: A Party Phantom lowers its empty plate and reaches toward its coat.
The Master raises a baton. A serving tray starts drifting after the guest.
ballroom.recap: A guest is ready to leave for another hall. The Master is preparing more music and food.

choices.label: Hold the coat where the guest can reach it.
lines: You hold the coat within reach. The phantom takes it and waves once.
The Master catches the following tray. Its baton dips before an encore can begin.
The guest walks into another hall of the House. The Master answers with one small wave.
choices.recap: You offered the coat. The guest left for another hall, and the Master ended the music and service for that visit.

choices.label: Return the guest’s goodbye wave.
lines: You give one goodbye wave. The phantom answers, takes its coat, and starts toward the next hall.
The Master looks at its baton, then sets it down and waves too.
It stops the serving tray from following. The guest leaves the Ballroom.
choices.recap: You returned the goodbye. The Master joined the farewell and let the guest leave for another hall.

choices.label: Leave the guest a clear way out.
lines: You leave space by the doorway. The phantom takes its coat and waves once.
The Master catches the serving tray before it can follow.

lines.speaker: The Master of Revels
lines.text: A tiny farewell flourish?

lines: It chooses one wave, puts down the baton, and lets the guest enter the next hall.
choices.recap: You kept the way clear. The Master stopped the encore and let the guest leave for another hall.

crypt.title: Room for the curl
lines: A curved spring bounces out of a straight groove between two display bones.
The Curator reaches to stretch it. Its own ribs make a roomy arch above the curl.
crypt.recap: The spring does not fit the straight display. The Curator is considering stretching it.

choices.label: Point from the curl to the Curator’s arched ribs.
lines: You point to the curl, then the arch. The Curator looks down at its own ribs.

lines.speaker: The Bone Curator
lines.text: Ah. Room at the ribs. Keep the bend.

lines: It moves the display bones into an arch. The spring settles beneath them, still curled.
choices.recap: You showed the matching arch. The Curator changed the display so the spring could keep its curl.

choices.label: Slide one loose display bone a little farther out.
lines: You widen the gap. The spring curls comfortably into the extra room.
The Curator moves the other display bone to make an arch above it.

lines.speaker: The Bone Curator
lines.text: More space. Fewer arguments with springs.

lines: It leaves the spring curled in the new display.
choices.recap: You widened the gap. The Curator completed an arched display around the spring’s unchanged curl.

choices.label: Watch how the spring settles.
lines: You wait. The spring bounces beneath the Curator’s arched ribs and settles into its curl.
The Curator looks from its ribs to the straight groove.

lines.speaker: The Bone Curator
lines.text: Ah. Keep the bend.

lines: It makes the display into an arch, leaving room for the curled spring.
choices.recap: You watched. The Curator learned from its own ribs and changed the display to fit the spring.

hedge-maze.title: Two useful things
lines: A mushroom pokes through the Gardener’s glove. The glove cannot close around its fork.
An empty pot and a broad fallen leaf rest on the bench.
hedge-maze.recap: A mushroom has grown through a useful glove. A pot and a patching leaf are nearby.

choices.label: Set the empty pot within reach.
lines: You set the pot beside the glove. The Gardener eases the mushroom into its new home.
It patches the glove with the fallen leaf and gives the mushroom a little water.

lines.speaker: The Gardener of Rot
lines.text: One pot. One glove. Two successes.

choices.recap: You offered the pot. The Gardener replanted the mushroom, repaired the glove and cared for both.

choices.label: Offer the broad leaf as a patch.
lines: You offer the leaf. The Gardener holds it against the hole, considering.
It moves the mushroom into the pot, patches the glove, and tries the fork again.

lines.speaker: The Gardener of Rot
lines.text: This one stays a glove.

lines: It waters the mushroom in its pot.
choices.recap: You offered a patch. The Gardener kept the useful glove and gave the mushroom a watered pot.

choices.label: Give the Gardener working room.
lines: You leave the bench clear. The Gardener tries the fork once more, then looks at the empty pot.
It replants the mushroom and patches the glove with the leaf.

lines.speaker: The Gardener of Rot
lines.text: This one stays a glove.

lines: It waters the mushroom. Both things have a place.
choices.recap: You gave the Gardener room. It repaired the glove and replanted and watered the mushroom.

secret-passages.title: Just one listener
lines: A resident taps a speaking tube. The taps clatter from every tube in the wall. The resident covers its ears.
A route switch sits above the resident’s reach.
secret-passages.recap: A resident’s call is being sent everywhere. The switch that selects a destination is too high.

choices.label: Point out the unreachable switch.
lines: You point to the switch. The Warden lowers it within the resident’s reach.
The resident aims it toward the quiet nook and taps again. Only the nook answers: three soft taps.

lines.speaker: The Whisper Warden
lines.text: I could repeat that for—oh. You heard.

lines: The switch stays within reach. The other tubes remain quiet.
choices.recap: You showed the unreachable switch. The resident can now choose a destination, and its call goes only there.

choices.label: Ask the Warden to listen without repeating.
lines: You ask the Warden to listen. In the pause, it notices the resident reaching toward the route switch.
It lowers the switch. The resident selects the quiet nook and taps three times.
Three soft taps answer from that nook alone. The Warden keeps its echo to itself.
choices.recap: You asked for a quiet listener. The Warden lowered the switch, and the resident chose the only destination for its call.

choices.label: Wait quietly for the resident.
lines: You stay quiet. The resident points at the high switch, then reaches again.
The Warden lowers it. The resident chooses the quiet nook and taps.
Only that nook answers. The Warden starts to echo, catches itself, and waits.
choices.recap: You waited for the resident. It gained control of the route switch, and its call reached only the chosen nook.

bathhouse.title: Beside the towel
lines: A little Puddle Spirit rests near a dry nook. The Matron holds a warm towel just above it.
The spirit edges sideways, toward the space beside the towel.
bathhouse.recap: The Puddle Spirit is making space beside the offered towel. The Matron has not put it down yet.

choices.label: Point to the empty space beside the spirit.
lines: You point to the space. The Matron sets the towel there, within reach.
The spirit rests beside it and stays there.

lines.speaker: The Drowned Matron
lines.text: Beside is also an option.

lines: Her hand moves away. The towel stays available.
choices.recap: You showed the empty space. The spirit chose to rest beside the towel, and the Matron left it undisturbed.

choices.label: Ask, “Could we leave it within reach?”
lines: The Matron lowers the towel into the nook instead of onto the spirit.
The spirit settles beside the towel, close enough to reach it.

lines.speaker: The Drowned Matron
lines.text: Beside. Yes. I can leave beside alone.

lines: She draws her hand back.
choices.recap: You asked for an offer within reach. The Matron left the towel beside the spirit and let it rest there.

choices.label: Give the spirit a little space.
lines: You wait clear of the nook. The spirit edges beside the Matron’s hovering towel again.
She notices and puts the towel down in the space it left.

lines.speaker: The Drowned Matron
lines.text: Beside is also an option.

lines: She keeps her hand out of the spirit’s way.
choices.recap: You gave the spirit space. The Matron put the towel within reach and let the spirit rest beside it.

kennels.title: An empty bed
lines: A ward animal noses toward the next hall. Its clean bed is behind it; its water bowl is in the doorway.
The Kennelmaster holds a folded blanket and looks between the animal and the empty bed.
kennels.recap: A ward animal wants to reach the next hall. Its bowl blocks the threshold, while its clean bed waits behind it.

choices.label: Slide the bowl clear of the threshold.
lines: You slide the bowl aside. The animal noses the clear threshold and steps into the next hall.
The Kennelmaster lays the blanket on the empty bed.

lines.speaker: The Kennelmaster
lines.text: An empty bed is not a failed bed.

lines: It leaves the fresh water beside the path, where it can still be reached.
choices.recap: You cleared the bowl from the doorway. The ward animal entered the next hall; its clean bed and water remained available.

choices.label: Help spread the loose corner of the blanket.
lines: You smooth the loose corner on the bed. The Kennelmaster looks at the animal waiting by the bowl.
It moves the bowl aside. The animal steps into the next hall.

lines.speaker: The Kennelmaster
lines.text: An empty bed is not a failed bed.

lines: The bed stays ready, with water beside the clear path.
choices.recap: You helped ready the bed. The Kennelmaster cleared the bowl, and the animal left for the next hall while care stayed available.

choices.label: Give the animal a clear space to wait.
lines: You leave room beside the animal. It noses toward the hall once more.
The Kennelmaster moves the bowl clear. The animal steps through the threshold.

lines.speaker: The Kennelmaster
lines.text: An empty bed is not a failed bed.

lines: It leaves the bed clean and the fresh water beside the path.
choices.recap: You gave the animal room. The Kennelmaster cleared its path to the next hall and kept its bed and water ready.

pumpkin-grounds.title: The pond is ready
lines: The King kneels by a marker marked HARVEST DATE. A frog turns toward the pond.
The King dips its brush, trying to decide what to write about the frog.
pumpkin-grounds.recap: The frog is heading toward the pond while the King tries to fit it into a harvest plan.

choices.label: Point the loose marker toward the pond.
lines: You turn the loose marker toward the water. The King looks along it.
It crosses out HARVEST DATE and writes POND THIS WAY.
The frog slips into the pond before the paint is dry.

lines.speaker: The Harvest King
lines.text: An early success.

choices.recap: You pointed toward the pond. The King replaced the harvest plan with a direction; the frog reached the water on its own.

choices.label: Tell the King where the frog is going.
lines: You tell the King the frog is heading for the pond. It looks up just as the frog reaches the water.

lines.speaker: The Harvest King
lines.text: Already? I had not finished the—

lines: It crosses out HARVEST DATE and writes POND THIS WAY, pointing the marker toward the pond.
The frog is comfortably ahead of the sign.
choices.recap: You drew attention to the frog’s route. The King replaced its harvest plan with a pond sign after the frog arrived.

choices.label: Let the frog go at its own pace.
lines: You wait. The frog slips into the pond while the King studies its brush.

lines.speaker: The Harvest King
lines.text: Frog? Pumpkin-frog? I cannot finish the label.

lines: It crosses out HARVEST DATE and writes POND THIS WAY.

lines.speaker: The Harvest King
lines.text: An early success.

choices.recap: You let the frog continue. The King replaced its harvest plan with a direction to the pond.

heart.title: Room at the threshold
lines: The Keeper’s hands hover near the locks. A loose fold of curtain lies across the way onward.
No animal is being moved toward the passage. The House waits.
heart.recap: The Keeper is hesitating at the locks. The way onward is still closed, and everyone has room to wait.

choices.label: Move the loose curtain away from the threshold.
lines: You draw the loose fold aside, leaving a clear space at the threshold.
The Keeper lowers its hands. The locks relax, and the way onward opens.

lines.speaker: The Keeper
lines.text: I must let them answer.

lines: Nothing is pushed through the opening.
choices.recap: You cleared the threshold. The Keeper stopped holding the locks, and the passage opened without moving anyone through it.

choices.label: Tell the Keeper, “We can wait here.”
lines: You offer to wait. The Keeper looks at the space before the door.
Its hands lower. The locks relax, and the passage opens.

lines.speaker: The Keeper
lines.text: I must let them answer.

lines: Nobody is hurried through the opening.
choices.recap: You offered to wait. The Keeper opened the passage and left everyone room to decide what comes next.

choices.label: Step back and leave the threshold clear.
lines: You leave space before the door. The Keeper lowers its hands from the locks.
The House grows quiet. A way onward opens without pulling anyone through.

lines.speaker: The Keeper
lines.text: I must let them answer.

choices.recap: You left space at the threshold. The Keeper stopped holding the passage shut, without pushing anyone through.
